key_result: Fine-tuned BGE-small improves NDCG@10 on all 5 BEIR datasets, up to +19.5% on NFCorpus (0.3304 to 0.3949), with 20.9 ms median search latency at 50K chunks.
notes: Inconsistencies: chunk size about 250 tokens (Sec 1.4.4) vs 1024 with 128 overlap (Sec 7.3); SciFact 295 queries (Sec 5.2) vs 300 (Sec 7.1/Table 2); BGE-small SciFact baseline 0.7263 (abstract/Table 3) vs 0.6464 (Tables 4,6); '3 of 5 datasets' differs for ColBERTv2 vs BGE-base; relevance-signal F1 0.856-0.996 (intro) vs 0.472-0.996 (Table 2); Sec 7.2 says hybrid strongest but Table 5a shows vector-only higher (0.832 vs 0.803); 74.5% disagreement is unweighted mean, pooled 71.8% (541/753); Table 9 '1K' and '5K' both 5,183 chunks; 50,425 'relevance-judged' queries include about 10K irrelevant per dataset; FiQA 648 vs 135 queries. No refusal mechanism, only distance-based confidence tiers; hardware not specified; ColBERTv2 comparison uncontrolled.

title: When Generic Prompt Improvements Hurt: Evaluation-Driven Iteration for LLM Applications
datasets: Three hand-authored suites (extraction 20 seeds, RAG 15, instruction 15) each expanded to 30 cases
models: Llama 3 8B Instruct (q4_K_M); Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct (q4_K_M) via Ollama 0.18.2
hardware: Mac mini M4, 16 GB unified memory
key_result: Appending generic rules to the user prompt cut Qwen 2.5 RAG citation/content-compliance from 26/30 to 9/30, while output-contract prompts raised strict extraction (Llama 3 0/30 to 28/30).
notes: Page read truncated at 100000 of about 160459 chars (later sections unseen). Inconsistencies: ablation uses 30 cases per task, below the paper's own recommended 50-200 golden set and 100 lower bound and its 400-600 needed to detect a 5-point difference; abstract says RAG compliance declines under some rule conditions but Llama 3 RAG rises under Rules (19/30 to 22/30) and declines only under Full/Non-conflicting (16/30). RAG suite is closed-context (no retriever); citation checks are must_cite proxies, not citation precision; abstention checked only via unknown-answer policy; no abstention rates seen.
